domain: Religious Studies / Japanese History / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of shinbutsu-shugo (Shinto-Buddhist syncretism) in pre-Meiji Japan as a potential contested kernel. The topic examines whether centuries of simultaneous practice represent a single fused ontological commitment or a domain-partitioned coexistence, testing whether the apparent kernel is coherent or an incoherent bundle masquerading as unity.

key_entities: Meiji state (1868 shinbutsu bunri separation policy)
Honji suijaku doctrine (kami as local manifestations of buddhas)
key_tensions: Ontological unity vs domain partition (whether syncretism is one commitment or two)
State enforcement vs popular practice (institutional vs vernacular syncretism)
key_mechanisms: Honji suijaku interpretive framework (buddhas as 'original ground', kami as 'trace manifestations')
Temple registration system (danka seido) enforcing Buddhist institutional dominance
Jinguji architectural fusion (shared ritual spaces, personnel, calendars)
key_absences: Absence of recorded cognitive dissonance in practitioner accounts (syncretism treated as natural, not contradictory)
Absence of systematic theological reconciliation texts (practice preceded and exceeded theory)

axes.human_readable: Syncretic Fusion Reading (One Fused Ontological Commitment)
axes.structural_delta: Kami and buddhas constitute a single integrated cosmology; honji suijaku is not metaphor but ontological truth
axes.primary_observable: Ritual practice treating kami-buddha distinction as internal to one system (e.g., single prayer addressing both without code-switching)
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; represents institutional and popular fusion position

axes.structural_delta: Kami govern this-world concerns (agriculture, purification, life transitions); buddhas govern afterlife and salvation; no ontological fusion required
axes.primary_observable: Ritual domain segregation (birth/marriage at shrines, funerals at temples; different prayer content)
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; represents functional coexistence without ontological commitment

axes.human_readable: Incoherent Bundle Reading (No Kernel, Only Institutional Drift)
axes.structural_delta: Syncretism is not a coherent commitment but accumulated institutional drift under state enforcement; practitioners hold contradictory beliefs without resolution
axes.primary_observable: Meiji separation's ease (rapid institutional disentanglement suggests no deep ontological fusion)
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; represents skeptical position that kernel is illusory

axes.human_readable: Meiji Separation as Structural Shock (Forced Disentanglement)
axes.structural_delta: 1868 shinbutsu bunri policy as state-imposed constraint forcing institutional separation
axes.primary_observable: Temple destruction rates, shrine purification campaigns, personnel reassignments 1868-1875
axes.selection_reason: Independent mountain axis; historical event testing kernel coherence but not itself a reading of the kernel

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Buddhist institutional dominance via honji suijaku interpretive hierarchy
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Captured within syncretic_fusion_reading as mechanism; not structurally independent

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Gap between elite theological discourse and popular ritual practice
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Cross-cuts all three readings; better addressed in omega as methodological uncertainty

omegas.description: Absence of recorded cognitive dissonance: did practitioners experience syncretism as one commitment, two, or neither? Elite texts silent; vernacular sources scarce. Reading selection depends on unrecoverable phenomenology.

Meiji separation's rapidity: does it prove incoherent_bundle (easy to separate because never fused) or domain_partition (institutional separation possible without ontological crisis)? Same observable supports two readings.

Core uncertainty: is shinbutsu-shugo one contested kernel with three readings, or three separate claims about an incoherent historical phenomenon? The D2 half-break test: if readings 1 and 2 both hold, does reading 3 collapse, or do all three coexist as legitimate interpretive positions?
Is honji suijaku a metaphysical claim (buddhas ontologically prior) or a political claim (Buddhist institutions hierarchically superior)? Same doctrine, different constraint types.

fracture_scan.notes: F34 detected: Model lacks deep expertise in Japanese religious history and phenomenology of practice. Readings derived from secondary historiography, not primary sources. Omega_practitioner_consciousness flags the core epistemic limit. Recommend domain expert review before generation.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Shinbutsu-shugo as shared ontological substrate: the claim that kami and buddhas constitute a single religious reality requiring simultaneous practice
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Interpretive authority distributed across: (1) honji suijaku doctrinal framework (Buddhist institutional), (2) jinguji ritual practice (syncretic institutional), (3) vernacular custom (non-textual)

readings.commitment: Kami and buddhas are ontologically unified; honji suijaku describes metaphysical truth, not institutional arrangement
readings.authority_grounding: Honji suijaku doctrine + jinguji institutional practice
readings.expected_structural_delta: High institutional entanglement; resistance to separation; syncretism as deep ontological commitment

readings.commitment: Kami and buddhas govern separate domains (this-world vs afterlife); coexistence is functional, not ontological
readings.authority_grounding: Ritual domain segregation + vernacular practice patterns
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low institutional entanglement; easy separation possible; syncretism as pragmatic coexistence

readings.commitment: No coherent kernel exists; syncretism is accumulated institutional drift under state enforcement, not a unified commitment
readings.authority_grounding: Meiji separation as natural experiment + skeptical historiography
readings.expected_structural_delta: Syncretism as snare: state benefits from enforced fusion; practitioners bear contradictory beliefs without resolution

axiom_contradictions.basis: Fusion reading requires ontological unity as metaphysical truth; bundle reading denies any coherent ontological commitment exists. No single framework holds both: either the unity is real or it is illusory institutional drift.
